What Needs You, on Home, holds the questions you need to answer and the notices that tell you what happened. A question has its answers as buttons, such as File It or Keep The Account, and Dismiss. A notice says what happened: groceries you couldn’t pay for, a commitment you slept through, a welcome to the school. The number beside Home on the menu counts both.

Where To Find It
Home, The What Needs You Panel.
When You Can Use It
From “What Needs You”.
Show Me Where
What To Press
Open Home and read What Needs You: questions first, then notices.
Press one of a question’s answers to act on it there. It does what the same button on its own screen does.
Press Go There to open the screen a question or a notice is about.
Press Dismiss to take a question off the list without answering it.
Press Mark N Read, at the top of the panel, to mark every unread notice read at once.
Press Show All N, under the notices, to see every unread one before you do: the panel draws the six most important first, and Show The Six Most Important goes back to them.
Press a question’s or a notice’s title to open it: how urgent or important it is, when it closes, and where it sits in the list.

Once you report a card lost or stolen, Chase declines anything new on it and sends a replacement with a new number. For a credit card, the account itself stays open and keeps its age on your credit record.

Chase watches cards around the clock and may text, send an app notification, email or call to check that unusual activity was you. Fraud alerts are automatic: you don’t need to sign up. The law on the debit card: If you report a lost or stolen debit card within two business days of finding out, you pay at most $50 of what was taken before you told the bank. After two business days, the most you pay rises to $500. And if a payment you didn’t make is on a statement and you don’t report it within 60 days of the statement being sent, you can be made to pay all of what’s taken after those 60 days. The two days start when you find out; the 60 days start when the statement is sent. This is Regulation E, 12 CFR 1005.6(b), under the Electronic Fund Transfer Act.

The law on the credit card: If someone uses your credit card without your permission, you pay at most $50, or less if less was spent before you told the card’s issuer. This is the Truth in Lending Act’s Regulation Z, 12 CFR 1026.12(b)(1)(ii).

The law on a payment you report as not yours: The bank has 10 business days to decide, or 20 for a payment in a new account’s first 30 days. If it needs longer, it must put the money back in your account for now within those 10 business days, and it can then take up to 45 days, or 90 for a debit card purchase, a payment made from outside the US or one on a new account.
